review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration of FairDICE operating successfully under non-convex scalarization functions.

claims.statement: FairDICE extends the DICE RL framework to optimize sample-based algorithms, balancing trade-offs between objectives and welfare under convexity assumptions.

support.explanation: Demonstrates how FairDICE builds on DICE RL to handle objective nonlinearities under specific assumptions.
support.passage: maximize welfare. Building on this, we extend the DICE RL framework to derive our sample based algorithm,FairDICE, that overcomes the optimization challenge caused by the nonlinearity of the objective.

review.alternative: Alternative dual formulations might bypass the convexity requirement without requiring structural changes.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that Lagrangian dual formulations can be extended to handle non-convex scalarization in MORL.

claims.statement: DICE-based approaches relying on Lagrangian duality assume convexity and do not cover all forms of non-convex scalarization.

support.explanation: Highlights the strict convexity limitation of current DICE-based multi-objective optimization methods.
support.passage: Our formulation assumes convexity, and thus the DICE-based approach relying on the Lagrangian dual does not apply to non-convex scalarization in MORL.

actions.findings:
FairDICE extends the DICE RL framework to optimize sample-based algorithms, balancing trade-offs between objectives and welfare under convexity assumptions. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]

DICE-based approaches relying on Lagrangian duality assume convexity and do not cover all forms of non-convex scalarization. [source-0bf4cf72590f4d6d]
actions.limitations: Current autonomous objective discovery mechanisms are heavily influenced by underlying optimization assumptions; while PC-PPO and FairDICE address certain scalarization and fairness limits, effective handling of broad non-convex scalarization and long-term, self-directed objective prioritization remains an open challenge.
actions.next_questions: How can DICE-based frameworks be extended to non-convex scalarization functions to support broader autonomous objective discovery?
actions.reason: Revising notebook findings to integrate FairDICE convex scalarization limits and multi-objective optimization constraints.
actions.summary: Autonomous systems increasingly utilize multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to pursue self-generated goals. Recent developments, specifically Pareto-Conditioned Proximal Policy Optimization (PC-PPO) and FairDICE, provide mechanisms to learn non-dominated policy portfolios and handle constrained optimization, allowing navigation of reliability-efficiency frontiers without retraining. However, the field still faces fundamental challenges regarding non-convex optimization and strict convexity assumptions in scalarization functions.
actions.title: Foundations of Autonomous Objective Discovery in Artificial Systems

proposal.summary: This cycle incorporates new evidence regarding FairDICE and constrained optimization into the notebook for autonomous objective discovery, evaluating the limitations of convex scalarization in multi-objective reinforcement learning.
proposal.title: Revising Autonomous Objective Discovery Mechanisms with FairDICE
